summary: Specializing in Tibetology, Buddhist studies, and philosophy, Matthew T. Kapstein earned his Ph.D. at Brown University under Roderick M. Chisholm and others. His career includes posts at the University of Chicago, Columbia University, and the École Pratique des Hautes Études.

Working in Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and religious studies, Matthew W. King earned his Ph.D. from the University of Toronto under doctoral supervisor Frances Garrett, having also studied under Khenpo Kunga Sherab and Thubten Champa.

Matthias Alexander Castrén specialized in linguistics and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He studied at the University of Helsinki and Imperial Alexander University (~1830–1836), later holding posts at both institutions from around 1851 to 1852.
Linguist Matthias de Vries studied at Leiden University (~1837–1843). He held academic posts at the University of Groningen (1849–1853) and Leiden University (1853–1891).

Matthias von Lexer worked in linguistics and Indology. He studied at Graz and Erlangen-Nuremberg, and under Albrecht Weber and Franz Bopp, later holding posts at St. Anne's Gymnasium, Freiburg, Würzburg (1868), and Munich (1890).

Matthieu Ricard works in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He studied at the Pasteur Institute under François Jacob and under traditional teachers Kangyur Rinpoche and Dilgo Khyentse Rinpoche, later serving as a board member of the Mind and Life Institute.

Specializing in Indology, Buddhist studies, and philosophy, Mattia Salvini earned his PhD at SOAS under Tadeusz Skorupski and studied under Ram Shankar Tripathi and K. Srinivasan. He held posts at International Buddhist College (~2010) and Mahidol University (~2011).

Mauli Chand Prasad specialized in Buddhist studies and linguistics. He completed a doctoral dissertation at Babasaheb Bhimrao Ambedkar Bihar University under B. Jinanand and U. Dharmaratna, and served as a Lecturer in Pali at Nava Nalanda Mahavihara (attested 1984).
Maureen L. P. Patterson was an Indology scholar and South Asia Librarian at the University of Chicago, with her post attested in 1984 and 2007.

Indologist and linguist Maurice Bloomfield studied at Furman, Yale, and Johns Hopkins (PhD), learning under William Dwight Whitney and Charles Rockwell Lanman. He spent his career as a professor at Johns Hopkins University from 1881 to 1926.

Linguist Maurice Grammont studied at the École Pratique des Hautes Études (~1888–1892) and under Ferdinand de Saussure (~1889–1891). He subsequently held a post at the University of Montpellier from around 1895 to 1939.
Specializing in Sinology and Tibetology, Maurice Jametel studied at the École nationale des langues orientales vivantes (~1875–1879), where he later held a post from around 1886 to 1889.
Working in Buddhist studies and linguistics, Maurice O'Connell Walshe studied under Walpola Rahula and held a post at the University of London from around 1947 to 1979.
Maurice Wiles was a religious studies scholar who studied at Tonbridge School (~1937–1941) and Christ's College, Cambridge (~1945–1950).

Maurine Stuart worked in Buddhist studies, having studied at the University of Manitoba and under teachers including Eido Shimano, Hakuun Ryoko Yasutani, and Soen Nakagawa. In 1979, she became president and spiritual director of the Cambridge Buddhist Association.

Mauro Maggi works in Iranian and Central Asian studies, linguistics, and Buddhist studies, having completed a doctoral thesis at the University of Naples "L'Orientale". His career includes roles at IsMEO, IsIAO, and Sapienza University of Rome (attested 2018).

Mavis L. Fenn studied at Winnipeg, Calgary, and McMaster (Ph.D. under Graeme MacQueen). A Buddhist and religious studies scholar, she held posts at St. Paul's University College (attested 2005–2006) and the University of Waterloo (attested 2016).

Max Deeg works in Indology, Buddhist studies, and Sinology. After completing his Habilitation at the University of Würzburg, he served as Head of School at Cardiff University (attested 2010–2021) and Research Fellow at the International Institute for Buddhist Studies (attested 2026).

Max Kaltenmark specialized in Sinology and religious studies. He directed the Centre Franco-Chinois d'Études Sinologiques (1946) and the École française d'Extrême-Orient (1949–1953), and held posts at the École Pratique des Hautes Études and the University of Paris.

Linguist and religious studies scholar Max Leopold Margolis received his Ph.D. from Columbia University in 1891. He held faculty posts at Hebrew Union College, the University of California, and Dropsie College, where he chaired biblical philology from 1909 to 1932.
